WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Enhancement build has been tested. Talent rows unlock at levels 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40. Every tree now carries a new single-point milestone talent at 16 points, alongside the familiar ones at 11, 21 and 31; which row it sits in varies by tree. No source has posted a level 30 build either — the cap only reached 30 on October 1 and none of the three has published one since — so the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended.

What Enhancement is for

Weapon imbues that now last an hour instead of five minutes. On levelling the published agreement is unusually clear: "Due to its added mobility, Enhancement will remain the preferred open world leveling spec." It is also the one build where two independent sources publish the same eleven points in the same order.

Mana is the limiter. "Enhancement's solo damage is already solid once it starts picking up early tools with Shocks & Fire Nova, but its Mana is a limiting factor… eventually when more points are available, it will likely round itself out into a very strong leveling spec." Ratings: Overall 3.5, Levelling 3.5, Mobility 4.5. It is the only Shaman spec rated highest on levelling, and all three score 4.5 for mobility.

Shamans cannot dual wield in Forever. Buy one big two-hander. If you have played a later expansion, unlearn that.

Stat priority

Weapon DPS on a slow two-hander, then Hit and Expertise, critical strike, Strength, Intellect, Agility, Spell Power, Spirit, Stamina.

Intellect ranks higher than you would expect, and a talent is why: "Mental DexterityMental DexterityTalentCastInstantIncreases your Attack Power by an amount equal to 100% of your Intellect. 3/3 turns a point of Intellect into 1 attack power with its mana beside it." So Intellect is damage and uptime here. One published list puts Strength and Intellect the other way round and is internally inconsistent about it; no source resolves the order, so taking the talent as the tiebreaker is our own reading.

On Enhancement tanking

You will see this discussed, so here is what is and is not known.

Spirit WeaponsSpirit WeaponsTalentCastInstantGives a chance to parry enemy melee attacks, reduces all threat generated by your attacks by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is not active, and increases all threat generated by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is active. is new. It takes the row-5 slot (level 30) where Classic had the plain ParryParryTalentCastInstantGives a chance to parry enemy melee attacks. talent, and it reads identically across three sources: "Gives a chance to parry enemy melee attacks, reduces all threat generated by your attacks by 30% while Rockbiter WeaponRockbiter WeaponSpell · NatureCastInstantCost15 ManaImbue the Shaman's weapon, increasing melee attack power by 29 and allowing melee attacks to cause additional threat when using that weapon. Lasts for 60 minutes. is not active, and increases all threat generated by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is active." Note the asymmetry one source alone flags: the reduction applies to your attacks; the increase applies to all threat you generate.

The three published positions:

  • For: "This talent alone allows Enhancement Shamans to perform off-tanking duties, or serve as tanks for dungeons in a pinch."
  • Partly for: Spirit WeaponsSpirit WeaponsTalentCastInstantGives a chance to parry enemy melee attacks, reduces all threat generated by your attacks by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is not active, and increases all threat generated by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is active. plus Improved Fire NovaImproved Fire NovaTalentCastInstant "will turn Shamans into formidable AoE tanks". But "The Shaman's survivability talents, however, are limited to AnticipationAnticipationTalentCastInstantIncreases your Defense Skill by 20. and ToughnessToughnessTalentCastInstantIncreases your Armor value from items by 10%.. That might not be enough to let them comfortably tank end-game dungeons and raids."
  • Against: "Parry and Rockbiter threat are not a reason to sign up as a raid tank; your damage build still needs a tank to hold dangerous group enemies."

There is no Blizzard statement either way: not in the Deep Dive recap, the What's Next recap, the class-design article, or the September 24 beta notes, and the relevant forum thread has no developer reply. Nor is there a published Blizzard taxonomy of tanks. Three tanks — Protection Warrior, Protection Paladin and Feral Druid — with Enhancement Shaman as damage is the working assumption in circulation, not Blizzard's: its Druid deep dive credits Druids with the "ability to serve any combat role", and its Hunter deep dive has pets tanking "in solo and small group play." Treat tanking as an experiment.

At level 60

Unknown — everything downstream of Maelstrom WeaponMaelstrom WeaponTalentCastInstant rank 5 and Rage of the Far Seer. Whether melee-into-instant-Bolt is a raid specialisation, and whether the Spirit WeaponsSpirit WeaponsTalentCastInstantGives a chance to parry enemy melee attacks, reduces all threat generated by your attacks by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is not active, and increases all threat generated by 30% while Rockbiter Weapon is active. threat mode has any sanctioned use, are both untested.
